gap: No result ChatGPT got puts a price on its own large-station picks alongside measured idle draw. Jackery's US store has the Explorer 2000 v2 at $999 on pre-order (ships Nov 16). Solar Lab measured 17 W idle (via wattpowerstation), and Best Batteries measured 1,920 Wh usable at an unstated load and port. A 15 W router on AC therefore gets about 1,920 ÷ (15 + 17) ≈ 60 h, or 2.5 days, not the 3–5 days ChatGPT showed. On the DC side, BLUETTI's US store now rates the $289.99 Elite 30 V2 at 4.5 W standby, half the 9 W the cited powerstations.reviews table attributes to BLUETTI.
standout_why: I compared against wattpowerstation.com/guides/portable-power-station-small-loads (cited), outagemath.com/appliances/wifi-router (cited), en.best-batteries.com restored-capacity-46-measurements (cited) and powerstations.reviews/guides/power-station-standby-draw (cited). wattpowerstation already has idle watts for the 2000 v2 (17 W) and the DELTA Pro 3 (49 W with AC on, about 13 W with DC only), but no prices and no router runtimes. outagemath lists 54 models with runtimes computed as Wh × 0.85 ÷ 15 W, with no idle draw and no prices. best-batteries has measured Wh but no idle or sub-20 W data and only UK prices. powerstations.reviews has only maker standby figures, no prices, and lists the Elite 30 V2 at 9 W. None of them combines today's US price with idle-adjusted hours. The parts already exist in those pages, so only the combination and the newer 4.5 W BLUETTI claim are new.
decides: This confirms that the big AC picks ChatGPT carded lose for a router. Their own idle draw (17 W for the Jackery 2000 v2; Jackery's listed 50 W for the 5000 Plus; 49 W with AC on for the DELTA Pro 3) is as big as or bigger than the router load, so dollars per hour of Wi-Fi are poor ($999 for about 60 h on AC). For the DC-only question it points to the small, cheap units run from DC: the EcoFlow TRAIL DC series (from $109; EcoFlow claims 0.01 W no-load) and the Anker SOLIX C300 DC. The BLUETTI Elite 30 V2 ($289.99, maker now claims 4.5 W standby) stays the pick when the router needs AC plus UPS switchover. I could not open a US price for the C300 DC or the TRAIL 300 DC variant, so the DC-only pick is unpriced.
